end.summary:
Asha practised sources of history, including objects and archaeological evidence.
Aarav repeatedly focused on written evidence and initially questioned what unwritten objects could show.
Asha practised ordering BCE dates; Aarav correctly ordered 500 BCE before later BCE dates in two unaided attempts.
Aarav correctly identified decade, century, and millennium as 10, 100, and 1,000 years.
Teach-back was not passed; no misconceptions were recorded.
end.parentNote: Asha practised how objects and other sources can provide evidence even when they have no writing, along with BCE timelines and time units. Aarav used the BCE rule correctly in two attempts and gave the meanings of decade, century, and millennium correctly. They kept returning to the idea that unwritten objects cannot give reliable information, and this was not fully corrected by the end of the lesson. At home, try sorting a few dates or events on a simple BCE-to-CE timeline and discuss what an object might show, even without words.

Haan, bilkul: decade das saal, century sau saal, aur millennium hazaar saal hota hai. Ab ek poster ki galti pakdiye: usmein likha hai ki Bharat 1947 mein, unneesveen century mein azaad hua. Ismein kya galat hai?
